title: Feature to display in the network applet the total amount of data sent/received
line: The Networks widget's Speed tab now shows how much data the connection has downloaded and uploaded in total.
explanation: The Networks widget already receives the device's total received and sent byte counters from NetworkManager, but only used them to compute the current speed, so the total amount of data used was never shown. The TrafficMonitor graph gains optional download/upload totals that are shown in its legend, e.g. "Download (132.4 GiB total)", and the applet passes the connection's counters to it.

commits.message:
applet: show total data sent and received in the Speed tab

The Speed tab only showed the current transfer rates, so there was no
way to see how much data a connection had used. The graph legend now
shows the total downloaded and uploaded data next to each direction.

BUG: 382830

patches.diff:
From 72da6d379cffe4bcf83c3a072a69d917b24838b5 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: =?UTF-8?q?Niccol=C3=B2=20Venerandi?= <niccolo@venerandi.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 22:06:51 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] applet: show total data sent and received in the Speed tab

The Speed tab only showed the current transfer rates, so there was no
way to see how much data a connection had used. The graph legend now
shows the total downloaded and uploaded data next to each direction.

BUG: 382830
---
 applet/ConnectionItem.qml   |  2 ++
 libs/qml/TrafficMonitor.qml | 11 ++++++++++-
 2 files changed, 12 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/applet/ConnectionItem.qml b/applet/ConnectionItem.qml
index e2a79fd2f..14446d4c5 100644
--- a/applet/ConnectionItem.qml
+++ b/applet/ConnectionItem.qml
@@ -211,6 +211,8 @@ PlasmaExtras.ExpandableListItem {
                     width: parent.width
                     downloadSpeed: connectionItem.rxSpeed
                     uploadSpeed: connectionItem.txSpeed
+                    downloadTotal: connectionItem.model.RxBytes
+                    uploadTotal: connectionItem.model.TxBytes
                 }
             }
 
diff --git a/libs/qml/TrafficMonitor.qml b/libs/qml/TrafficMonitor.qml
index 7b7224038..e4a119e81 100644
--- a/libs/qml/TrafficMonitor.qml
+++ b/libs/qml/TrafficMonitor.qml
@@ -15,6 +15,9 @@ import org.kde.kirigami as Kirigami
 ColumnLayout {
     property alias downloadSpeed: download.value
     property alias uploadSpeed: upload.value
+    // Total bytes transferred, shown in the legend when not negative.
+    property real downloadTotal: -1
+    property real uploadTotal: -1
 
     spacing: Kirigami.Units.largeSpacing
 
@@ -131,7 +134,13 @@ ColumnLayout {
             PlasmaComponents3.Label {
                 id: legendLabel
                 font: Kirigami.Theme.smallFont
-                text: model.name
+                text: {
+                    const total = index === 0 ? uploadTotal : downloadTotal;
+                    if (total < 0) {
+                        return model.name;
+                    }
+                    return i18nc("@label legend entry: %1 is Download or Upload, %2 is the total amount of data", "%1 (%2 total)", model.name, KCoreAddons.Format.formatByteSize(total));
+                }
                 textFormat: Text.PlainText
             }
         }
-- 
2.53.0

media.caption: Speed tab of the active Wi-Fi connection: the legend only says Upload and Download.
Same tab with the fix: the legend shows the total uploaded and downloaded data.

reviews.text: Clean, minimal QML change that exposes optional downloadTotal and uploadTotal properties on TrafficMonitor (defaulting to -1 so other callers like mobile KCMs stay unchanged) and binds them to RxBytes/TxBytes in ConnectionItem. Displaying the totals in the Speed tab legend keeps the UI compact, updates live with the graph, uses proper i18nc context and KCoreAddons.Format.formatByteSize, and is well-verified by screenshots and sysfs counters.

Brings back the KDE4 feature the reporter asked for: the Networks widget now shows total data received and sent for the active connection, using the RxBytes/TxBytes counters the model already had (refreshed every 2 s while the Speed tab is live). The change is small and opt-in: TrafficMonitor gets optional totals that default to -1, so the mobile KCMs stay as they are. The legend order (index 0 = Upload) matches the chart's valueSources, the new string has a translator context, and the screenshot shows sensible totals. Nitpicks: the counters are per-interface since it came up (not strictly 'since connecting' for modems whose wwan interface stays up), and the first frame may briefly read 0 B before NetworkManager's first statistics update. Neither blocks the feature.
